raw_response:
I plant like my neighbors plant. I been doing this long time, I know what works in our village.

My 8 mu — I put 3 mu for cotton on the sandy piece, and 5 mu I do wheat then maize, like everyone here does.

**Wheat** (the big winter crop):
I put down 2 bags of compound fertilizer before ploughing, that's one bag each half-mu. Then when the wheat turn green in spring I spread 1 bag of urea per mu, maybe a little more if the leaves look pale. My father-in-law always said "feed the wheat in spring or it won't fill." I water 3 times — once before winter so roots don't die, once at green-up, once when the ears come out. If bugs come I spray, usually 2 times. I use the same seed the seed shop sell everyone, improved kind, not the old village seed.

**Maize** after wheat:
I don't plough, just push the seed in right after wheat harvest, time is short, rain coming. One bag compound at planting, one bag urea when it come to my knee. Water 2 times if the rain don't come. Spray once for the borer worm. I buy hybrid seed, everyone does, the old seed give nothing.

**Cotton** on the sandy 3 mu:
Cotton eat a lot but my land is poor there. 1 bag compound before planting, half bag urea at squaring, half bag at boll. Water 3 times. Cotton got many bugs — I spray 6 times, sometimes 7, my neighbor spray 8. If I spray less the bollworm eat everything. I use the improved seed with the bug-resist in it, cheaper spraying.

I don't waste money but I don't short the fertilizer either. Bad harvest is worse than spending extra 100 yuan on urea.
